suggestions.title: A `<!--` inside a code span or fenced block hides every later evidence link
suggestions.failurePath:
Input body: "The parser skips `<!--` comments.

## Verified

[a](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/<40-hex>/docs/verify/1404/a.txt)". visibleText treats the `<!--` in the code span as an unclosed comment and drops the rest of the body, so parseRawEvidenceLinks returns {links: [], others: []}. GitHub renders the code span literally and shows the link (confirmed in the harness; a fenced ```html block containing `<!--` behaves the same way). GitHub hides the rest of the body only when `<!--` opens an HTML block at the start of a line. So the comment at lines 4-5 ("没闭合的 `<!--` 让 GitHub 吞掉后文") is too broad, and so is the PR body's "as GitHub renders it". This is the strict side, and Risk mentions "mid-line". But any PR that quotes `<!--` in backticks before its Verified section will read as having no evidence once S4 wires this in. #1420's own body is one: its Risk section quotes `<!--` at offset 20495 and everything after it is dropped.

suggestions.title: A link reference definition counts as rendered evidence
suggestions.failurePath: Body "[a]: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/<40-hex>/docs/verify/1404/a.txt" (a reference definition that nothing uses). GitHub renders nothing for it, but the parser returns links=[{sha, path:'docs/verify/1404/a.txt'}]. This is the lax side of the same "count only what GitHub renders" rule that excludes comments. The file still has to exist at that SHA, so the impact is small: a reviewer simply cannot see the link.

A PR that deletes the chief merge_builds rejection also passes with nothing flagged, and with D6 self-update that removes the human-only guard for every human-policy project. Nothing calls the gate today and every project is human, so there is no failure at this head.
